findings.message: `proj.web.trends` is partitioned by `refresh_date`, but the query doesn't filter on it, so it reads every partition (3.2 GB in all).
findings.fix: Add a filter on `refresh_date`, for example `refresh_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)`.

findings.message: `u` (users) and `t` (trends) are joined only by `t.refresh_date > u.signup_date`, which isn't an equality between two sources, so BigQuery compares every pair: about 219.9 trillion pairs. Bytes billed don't grow, but compute does, and counts or sums over the result are multiplied.
findings.fix: Add an equality between the two sides alongside the comparison, so BigQuery matches rows by it before comparing.
